questions.question_text: Which of the following is (are) the reason(s) that delay(s) the conduct of the kind of research that might enable nonmanualized individual psychotherapy to reach the current criteria for being "evidence based"?

options.text: Difficulty in getting funding and institutional approval
Difficulty in locating proper comparison groups
Difficulty in following control subjects as long as some individual cases actually take in therapy

questions.explanation: All of the listed reasons along with difficulty in getting parental and child consents have led to only a few clinical case series and a handful of controlled research projects in this field over many years.

questions.question_text: All of the following tactics for working with parents in parent counseling should be recommended except:

options.text: Guide parents to understand the purposes of consequences and to find an appropriate consequence that works for the child.
Model appropriate parent-child interactions for the parents to follow.
Encourage parents to receive therapy for themselves.
Eliminate using any punishment and replace it with rewards.
Refer parents to receive other needed services that you cannot provide.

correct_answer.text: Eliminate using any punishment and replace it with rewards.

correct_answers.text: Eliminate using any punishment and replace it with rewards.

questions.explanation: Appropriate punishment should not be eliminated, but the importance of counterbalancing punishment with rewards should be emphasized to the parents. Other tactics may include: assist parents to reframe the problems in a way that seems manageable and does not place responsibility solely on them; provide parents with supplemental materials for them to review outside of the sessions; and remind parents to be patient with gradual small incremental progress made without a quick cure.

questions.question_text: All of the following are advantages that multifamily psychoeducation groups have in comparison to individual family psychoeducation except:

options.text: Identification with other families and learning from others' success
Cost-effective and delivered in a large clinic
Chance to discuss and share with both professionals and other families

questions.explanation: Along with privacy, ease of being implemented by a private practitioner, scheduling flexibility, and flexibility in tailoring topics to meet individual special needs are the advantages that individual family psychoeducation has over the multifamily psychoeducation groups.

questions.question_text: All of the following are appropriate age adjustments needed for psychoeducation targeting children and adolescents with mental illness compared to those programs targeting adults except:

options.text: Higher intensity of service and longer follow up
Emphasizing the important aspects of the home environment

questions.explanation: All listed are appropriate age adjustments needed for psychoeducation targeting children and adolescents with mental illness compared to those programs for adults. In addition, because children may not have developed a healthy identity separate from the psychiatric symptoms that they suffer it is important to clarify with the child and family what the disorder is and what the child's traits are. With variable levels of development, developmentally appropriate contents should be used in different age groups.

questions.question_text: All of the following are psychoeducation core concepts except:
questions.explanation: Behavioral activation (not inhibition) is one of the core concepts of psychoeducation along with others such as types of disorders and symptoms, medication and side effects, problem-solving skills, treatment and services, and communication skills.

questions.question_text: All of the following are examples of techniques used in psychoeducation except:
questions.explanation: Naming the enemy (not friend) is one of the techniques used in psychoeducation to help the child and parents distinguish the difference between the child's symptoms and his/her own personality. Bibliotherapy refers to the usage of written information, video, and resources from media and the Internet to further educate families. Daily routine tracking and mood charts can help tracking daily routine activities such as sleep-wake cycles, eating, changes in mood, and how different activities or circumstances influence mood. "Thinking, feeling, doing" helps in gaining the insight of parents and child into the connections among their thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. Another technique called "tool kit" refers to the development of a series of pleasure and relaxing activities for the child to use in helping affective regulation.

questions.question_text: It is not uncommon for the leaders of a parent group or support group to face some challenges and difficult situations. Which of the responses by the group leaders should be excluded if one parent dominates the discussion?

options.text: Reminding the group of time and schedule
Setting amount of time for people to take turns
Thanking the parent who is sharing and asking if others would like to talk

questions.explanation: All of the listed responses are appropriate in this situation. There are many other frequent challenges and situations group leaders may face, such as arguing among members, crying, discussion of inappropriate topics, discussion shifts away from the scheduled topic, incomplete homework, late arrival, non-participation, lack of time to cover the topic, only one attendee, and cultural sensitivity all predict positive response and outcome.

questions.question_text: Setting treatment goals is an important step of behavioral parent training. All of the following are appropriately applicable to the discussion of establishing initial treatment goals between the therapist and the parent except:

options.text: Eliciting the parent's goal (commonly involves modifying child's behavior)
Explicitly identifying the parent's behavior that causes the child's problems
Finding a goal that is the best fit between parenting practices and the child's personality
Setting the initial goal at a level where both child and parent can experience success

correct_answer.text: Explicitly identifying the parent's behavior that causes the child's problems

correct_answers.text: Explicitly identifying the parent's behavior that causes the child's problems

questions.explanation: Modifying or changing the parent's behavior can be somehow discussed although this goal may not need to be explicitly stated because the therapist needs to communicate in a way to avoid the parent feeling that she or he is to blame for the child's behavior.

questions.question_text: In regards to behavioral parent training, a concept of 'coercive process' was proposed by Patterson (1982). Which of the following descriptions best explains its meaning?

options.text: External factors influence both children's and parents' behavior
Children's behavior controls the parents' reactions
Parents and children with behavioral problems control each other through negative reinforcement

correct_answer.text: Parents and children with behavioral problems control each other through negative reinforcement

correct_answers.text: Parents and children with behavioral problems control each other through negative reinforcement

questions.explanation: The theory behind behavioral parent training programs is based on the belief that dysfunctional parent-child relationship and interaction patterns are possible driving forces of the child's behavior problems. As a learned process, "coercive process" describes those families with a child having behavioral issues that have a tendency to control one another through negative reinforcement.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding the effectiveness and efficacy of behavioral parent training (BPT) are accurate based on updated research except:

options.text: BPT effectiveness does not extend to untreated siblings.
BPT improves parenting skills; improvements of child behavior are associated with the degree of changes in parenting.
Family-centered behavioral interventions are effective for adolescents.
BPT is effective in treating disruptive behavior disorders during preschool and elementary school.

correct_answer.text: BPT effectiveness does not extend to untreated siblings.

correct_answers.text: BPT effectiveness does not extend to untreated siblings.

questions.explanation: Research supports that BPT effectiveness can be extended to the untreated siblings. BPT does have positive effects on parent functioning, which leads to lower parenting stress, marital conflicts, depression; unifying childrearing approaches; gaining parental confidence in managing their child's behavior; and extending benefits to untreated siblings. Parents are more likely to report high levels of satisfaction with this approach.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding the factors that can influence the outcomes of BPT are accurate except:

options.text: Lower level of socioeconomic status (SES) predicts poorer overall outcome.
Lower level of SES predicts differentially more dropouts for behavior therapy versus other psychosocial interventions.
Severity and nature of the child's symptoms strongly influence outcome.
Parental psychopathology, parental involvement with illicit drugs, and severe marital discord all predict reduced efficacy.
Involvement of both parents in treatment may not affect outcome, but may increase the maintenance of treatment gains.

correct_answer.text: Lower level of SES predicts differentially more dropouts for behavior therapy versus other psychosocial interventions.

correct_answers.text: Lower level of SES predicts differentially more dropouts for behavior therapy versus other psychosocial interventions.

questions.explanation: Lower level of SES predicts early termination from the treatment, but it does not differentially predict more dropouts for behavior therapy in comparison to other psychosocial interventions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following family therapies emphasizes in-session interaction?
questions.explanation: Represented by Carl Whitaker and Virginia Satir, experiential family therapy emphasizes the in-session interactions, and tends to guide a conflicted parent-dyad to talk about the problems in the session. This approach demonstrates that the recognition of the here-and-now experience of family members is beneficial to the treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following concepts is most closely associated with Winnicott's theory?
questions.explanation: Holding environment is a critical component of D. W. Winnicott's theory. This refers to the caregivers providing a safe and nurturing environment to fulfill the child's needs and to facilitate the child's normal growth and development.

questions.question_text: Among all of the following models of family therapy, which is the newest one?
questions.explanation: Several newer models of family therapy have been developed to meet the clinical challenges we are facing today. Integrative module-based family therapy is one such model among two others including multisystemic therapy (MST) and meta-frameworks.

questions.question_text: Interpersonal psychotherapy for depressed adolescents (IPT-A) is not recommended for adolescents with all of the following conditions except:
questions.explanation: Research shows adolescents with depression can respond to IPT-A even when the depression is comorbid with anxiety disorder, ADHD, and ODD. However, the treatment is most effective when the primary diagnosis is depression with limited comorbidities, and it is not recommended for some of the conditions listed in answers (A) through (D).

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding IPT-A are accurate except:

options.text: IPT-A includes three phases: initial, middle, and termination.
IPT is based on interpersonal theories and attachment theory.
IPT-A, a time-limited and manualized psychotherapy, was originally adapted from IPT for adults.
Assigning the adolescent with a "limited sick role" is recommended during psychoeducation.

questions.explanation: Parental participation is highly encouraged, but not mandatory or required. Parental participation can be helpful at different phases of the treatment (e.g., education about depression and IPT-A treatment itself during the initial phase, providing opportunities to practice during the middle phase, and education about warning signs of depression recurrence in the termination phase).

questions.question_text: During the initial phase of IPT-A, the therapist helps the client identify interpersonal problem areas. If an adolescent's depression coincides with a relationship conflict, which of the following problem areas should be primarily identified?

options.text: Grief due to the death of a loved one

questions.explanation: Interpersonal role disputes should be identified in this case because the depression coincides with a relationship conflict, and resolving such a conflict is the goal of the treatment. In general, only one of the four listed areas needs to be identified, but it is also possible to identify a secondary problem area. Adolescents with interpersonal role dispute may fall into one of the following stages: renegotiation stage, impasse stage, and dissolution stage. During the first two stages, the therapist should assist the adolescent to define and to resolve the dispute. However, the treatment strategy will be focused on mourning the loss of the relationship if the adolescent is in the dissolution stage.

questions.question_text: Which of the following techniques is not commonly used in the middle phase of IPT-A?

options.text: Encouragement of affect and linkage with interpersonal events

questions.explanation: Transference interpretation is not commonly used in the middle phase of IPT-A. Instead, all of the other techniques listed can be appropriately used in the middle phase of IPT-A.

questions.question_text: Which of the following therapy modalities meets the American Psychological Association Division 12 criteria for a "well-established" psychotherapy for depression in youth?
questions.explanation: Among all the listed therapy modalities, IPT-A is the only one that meets the American Psychological Association Division 12 criteria for a "well-established" psychotherapy for depression in youth.

questions.question_text: During a session involving cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) for anxiety disorder, the therapist suggests the patient remain in contact with the feared stimulus until physiological response and subjective distress dissipate. Which of the following techniques best fits this description?
questions.explanation: Exposure is the key element of CBT for anxiety. Graduated exposure involves introducing the situation that elicits a low level of fear, followed by gradually introducing situations that elicit more intense fear; eventually the fearful behaviors or responses are eliminated (extinction). In a session when the fear-producing situation remains until the individual's fear response extinguishes, the process is called within-session habituation. If the individual is exposed to the situation that elicits the highest fear (not graduated) over repeated treatment sessions and the fear response dissipates, this process is called between-session habituation. Graduated exposure is more often reserved for younger children, whereas adolescents may be able to tolerate more intensive exposure techniques. Implosion therapy refers to utilizing horrifiing, frightening, and psychodynamic cues to enhance and maximize fear response and arousal state in order to achieve rapid extinction. Studies show this approach is often ineffective, and may be even countertherapeutic.

questions.question_text: Which of the following specific intervention(s) is (are) commonly used in cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) for depression?
questions.explanation: All are specific interventions commonly used in CBT among others including introduction and treatment rationale, goal setting, mood monitoring, rational problem-solving, rationally disputing automatic thoughts and replacing them with adaptive self-statements, correction of cognitive distortions, social skills training, communication and compromise, parent training, booster sessions, and relapse prevention.

questions.question_text: All of the following factors clearly predict poor outcomes of CBT in the treatment of depression among adolescents except:
questions.explanation: There are conflicting data regarding whether comorbidity predicts a poor outcome. In addition, lower level of suicidal ideation, higher overall baseline functioning, consistency in completing homework, therapeutic warmth, responsiveness, and planning ahead/anticipating future behavior problems predict positive response and outcome.

questions.question_text: All of the following are applied behavior analysis (ABA) techniques used as interventions for children with autism spectrum disorders except:
questions.explanation: Backward chaining is an ABA technique, which refers to a complex behavior that is taught by starting with reinforcing the successful performance of the final step, and working backward one step after another to the initial step of the behavior. The goal is to eventually reinforce the child being able to perform the whole behavior.

questions.question_text: Which of the following stages should be excluded from systematic desensitization commonly used in the treatment of anxiety?
questions.explanation: The choices comprise the four stages of systemic desensitization and none of them should be excluded.

questions.question_text: All of the following are developmental advantages that adolescents may possess in favor of the motivational interviewing (MI) approach except:
questions.explanation: Lack of discrepancies is a challenge to using MI in adolescents because assisting an adolescent to examine discrepancies with risk-taking behavior may backfire if the adolescent is in denial.

questions.question_text: In a recent study by S. N. Merry et al. (2012), which of the following symptoms was treated with a computerized self-help intervention, Smart, Positive, Active, Realistic, X-factor thoughts (SPARX), and did not show inferiority to treatment as usual?
questions.explanation: Smart, Positive, Active, Realistic, X-factor thoughts (SPARX) is a computerized cognitive behavior therapy model. The study is a randomized controlled non-inferiority trial that compared SPARX to treatment as usual (face-to-face counseling delivered by trained counsellors and clinical psychologists) for adolescents seeking help for depression. The symptom reduction of the SPARX group was not inferior to treatment in the as usual group, and SPARX groups had a higher remission rate. The authors concluded that SPARX is a potential alternative treatment option to conventional treatment.

questions.question_text: Match the treatment name with the best treatment description. Functional family therapy

options.text: Interrupting rigid feedback, maintaining the family homeostasis, and strengthening the parental alliance using paradoxical instructions
Emphasizing the establishment of boundaries within the family
Addressing the function of symptoms in family interaction, enhancing supportive interactions, and reducing defensive interactions
Focusing on the "unconscious" life of the family members, disentangling interlocking alliances

correct_answer.text: Addressing the function of symptoms in family interaction, enhancing supportive interactions, and reducing defensive interactions

correct_answers.text: Addressing the function of symptoms in family interaction, enhancing supportive interactions, and reducing defensive interactions

questions.explanation: Functional family therapy is an intensive home-based approach, and is designed to address the function of symptoms in family interactions. The goals are to enhance supportive interactions and to reduce defensive interactions.

questions.question_text: Match the treatment name with the best treatment description. Psychodynamic family therapy

options.text: Emphasizing the establishment of boundaries within the family
Focusing on the "unconscious" life of the family members, disentangling interlocking alliances
Interrupting rigid feedback, maintaining the family homeostasis, and strengthening the parental alliance using paradoxical instructions
Addressing the function of symptoms in family interaction, enhancing supportive interactions, and reducing defensive interactions

correct_answer.text: Focusing on the "unconscious" life of the family members, disentangling interlocking alliances

correct_answers.text: Focusing on the "unconscious" life of the family members, disentangling interlocking alliances

questions.explanation: Psychodynamic family therapy focuses on the "unconscious" life of family members and encourages them to share their unconscious conflicts and defenses, and intra-familial transference reactions in the therapy. Psychodynamic family psychotherapy is good for families with long-standing but subtle symptoms, and it can be combined with individual therapies.

questions.question_text: Match the treatment name with the best treatment description. Strategic family therapy

options.text: Interrupting rigid feedback, maintaining the family homeostasis, and strengthening the parental alliance using paradoxical instructions
Addressing the function of symptoms in family interaction, enhancing supportive interactions, and reducing defensive interactions
Focusing on the "unconscious" life of the family members, disentangling interlocking alliances
Emphasizing the establishment of boundaries within the family

correct_answer.text: Interrupting rigid feedback, maintaining the family homeostasis, and strengthening the parental alliance using paradoxical instructions

correct_answers.text: Interrupting rigid feedback, maintaining the family homeostasis, and strengthening the parental alliance using paradoxical instructions

questions.explanation: Strategic family therapy sees families in terms of process and maladaptive problem-solving efforts. In the therapy, strategies should be developed to identify the family rules, interrupt rigid feedback, strengthen the parental alliance, and maintain the family's homeostasis.

questions.question_text: Match the treatment name with the best treatment description. Structural family therapy

options.text: Addressing the function of symptoms in family interaction, enhancing supportive interactions, and reducing defensive interactions
Focusing on the "unconscious" life of the family members, disentangling interlocking alliances
Interrupting rigid feedback, maintaining the family homeostasis, and strengthening the parental alliance using paradoxical instructions
Emphasizing the establishment of boundaries within the family

correct_answer.text: Emphasizing the establishment of boundaries within the family

correct_answers.text: Emphasizing the establishment of boundaries within the family

questions.explanation: Structural family therapy focuses on adaptive and maladaptive structure, particularly in relation to power, boundaries, and preferred transactional patterns. Reestablishing and realigning family boundaries are emphasized in the therapy.
